wars.outcome: The Allied offensive of September 1918 (bombardment from 14 September; 'the following day, the French and Serbians attacked and captured their objective' at Dobro Pole) broke the Bulgarian line; 'By 29 September (a day before Bulgaria exited World War I), Skopje fell'; the Bulgarians were granted the Armistice of Salonica on 29 September and the front ended 'at noon on 30 September 1918'.
wars.note: The war is entered from 1918, the year the dossier's life begins; the Serbian army's earlier part on the Macedonian front (refit on Corfu, the abandonment of Bitola by the Central Powers by 19 November of the 1916 campaign) and the campaigns of 1914-1915 belong to the serbs dossier. The page gives no date for the army's arrival at Salonika, so none is stated here.
